claims.exact_claim: Weak admissibility together with the finite local-field descent stipulated in the manuscript implies admissibility, including residue characteristic two.
claims.version_relation: Same natural statement and context; v2 adds CF-WA as an external assumption, not a second result.
hypotheses: k=Fpbar and K0=Frac W(k); the filtration is over a finite extension K/K0.
There is a finite extension H/Qp with maximal unramified subfield H0=Frac W(Fp^f), embedded compatibly so that H0 is contained in K0 and L=K0H is contained in a common finite extension K/K0.

A finite-dimensional H0-isocrystal D0 with invertible sigma-semilinear Frobenius and N=0, a separated exhaustive decreasing filtration on H tensor_H0 D0, and the rational tensor data descend together.
A Frobenius- and tensor-compatible identification K0 tensor_H0 D0=D_x identifies the filtration after scalar extension from H.
Weak admissibility means total Hodge/Newton equality and the inequality for every Frobenius subobject of the faithful filtered isocrystal.
claims.assessment: The stipulated rational implication is supported; its integral and geometric surroundings are not conclusions of this unit.

decisive_argument: Every phi0-stable H0-subspace extends faithfully to a phi-stable K0-subspace; no assertion that all K0-subobjects descend is needed.
Flat extension commutes with the induced-filtration intersections and preserves graded dimensions, hence t_H.
With v_p(p)=1, t_N=v_p(det A) for the semilinear Frobenius matrix A is unchanged. Over H0 of residue degree f, v_p(det phi0^f)=f*t_N; the f-iterate expression must be divided by f.
Weak admissibility over K0 therefore implies weak admissibility of the descended H0/H object.
CF Theorem A over H supplies a semistable representation; N=0 and B_cris=B_st^(N=0) make it crystalline.
Crystalline and filtered de Rham comparison base-change via L=K0H and the common finite extension K, recovering exactly D_x and the prescribed filtration.
CF's complete-DVR, characteristic-zero, perfect-residue-characteristic-p>0 setup contains no odd-prime exclusion.
supported_scope: PF-WA v1-v2 as a conditional application of Colmez-Fontaine Theorem A.
The last sentence of lem:admissible-realization, supplying only its rational admissibility condition (1).
Correction of the retired route's logical direction: rational admissibility precedes geometric realization.
limitations: Finite local-field descent is stipulated, not automatic for a filtration over a finite extension of K0.
H need not be contained in K0; scalar extension uses K0H, not a fictitious finite extension K0/H.
No canonical integral lattice, integral defining tensors on every stable lattice, integral frame torsor, abelian lift, or exact fixed quasi-isogeny is obtained from Theorem A.
No assessment of KZ/PR/GLX geometric steps or their p=2 hypotheses is made here.
The author-version text and journal pagination are distinct; DOI metadata was not externally revalidated.
concrete_obligations: For any application, supply the simultaneous Frobenius/tensor/filtration descent identification, not just a finite field of definition over K0.
Use all Frobenius subobjects and consistent Hodge/Newton normalizations.
Treat integral lattice and exact-marking abelian realization as separate geometric obligations.
